alex: FYI I recorded an nsys trace after noticing a perf regression on matmul path post-commit 9f2b7a3. p95 for seq=1024,batch=1 on A100 (fp16) is ~+10%. timeline shows repeated cudaMalloc/cudaFree spikes interleaved with GEMM kernels and some launch serialization.

priya: can you share the nsys cmd + the NVTX snapshot? curious if cublasLt probe returned a different algo.

alex: nsys cmd I used: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --output=/tmp/trace-matmul-1867`
NVTX notes: probe picks algoId=127 (workspace=30MB) then lots of launches fall back to algoId=41 (no workspace). between the switch there9s a ~40-60ms window with many cudaMalloc/free events. looks like workspace allocation churn.

yuan: that matches a scenario where the workspace query succeeds but we don't have a persistent buffer and end up cudaMallocing per-launch. also if KV cache allocations interleave we can fragment our slab and trigger cudaMalloc.

alex: paste from heuristic trace:
```
heuristic: algo=127 requiredWorkspace=31457280 status=SUCCESS
heuristic: algo=41 requiredWorkspace=0 status=FALLBACK_NO_WS
kernel launch: algo=127 time=54us
kernel launch: algo=41 time=83us
cudaMalloc(31457280) -> 0
cudaFree -> 0
```
But nvprof timeline shows malloc/free happening across many kernels, not just once.

chris: recall PR #512 changed packer to more aggressively coalesce sequences; that could push peak workspace > slab size and then we lose reuse.

priya: also saw KV cache warmup causing small allocations right before the workspace mallocs. mixing allocation sizes can fragment our buffer pool.

perf-bot: regression alert: redwood-qa/llama-13b seq1024 batch1 p95 +9.4% vs baseline (2026-03-10). trace uploaded s3://redwood-perf/matmul/1867012345/nsys.tar.gz

alex: repro steps I used:
```
# repro harness
python perf/repro.py --seq 1024 --batch 1 --dtype fp16 --device 0 --capture nsys
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --capture-range=nvtx --output=matmul-1867
```

yuan: mitigation options I9d try: 1) add a persistent per-device workspace buffer to avoid cudaMalloc/free; 2) cap per-request workspace (e.g., 64MB) so the probe prefers smaller algos under latency SLO; 3) separate allocator pools for KV cache vs workspace; 4) tweak packer to avoid packing sequences that would blow workspace.

chris: +1 for persistent buffer + packer guard. also we could alter probe heuristic to penalize algorithms requiring large temp workspace when tail latency is important.

priya: please file an issue with nsys + perfetto snapshots and link s3 artifacts. ping me and @yuan on the ticket.

alex: filed ENG-RUNTIME-687 (assigned to @yuan). attached s3 link and NVTX screenshots. I9m going to roll a temporary config override setting workspace_limit=64MB for the canary.

yuan: taking ENG-RUNTIME-687. plan: reproduce locally, implement persistent workspace pool, add an e2e perf test, then tweak probe heuristics. ETA EOD tomorrow.

alex: thanks. keep perf-bot alerts on; post before/after traces in the ticket. :thumbsup:
